t: A Dutch plantation colony on the Guiana coast, taken from the English in 1667 and run for a century by the Society of Suriname.
Enslaved Africans worked its sugar and coffee estates; runaways formed maroon nations that won peace treaties in the 1760s.
Indentured Asian migrants made it highly diverse; it became independent in 1975 and has been a democracy since 1991.
dyk: Under the Treaty of Breda of 1667 the Dutch kept Suriname while the English kept New Amsterdam, which they had renamed New York.
ev: A Zeeland fleet captures the English colony, confirmed as Dutch by the Treaty of Breda
The Society of Suriname takes over the colony
The colony makes peace with the Ndyuka maroons
Slavery is abolished on 1 July, now commemorated as Keti Koti
The first indentured labourers from British India arrive
Suriname becomes an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands
Sergeants led by Desi Bouterse seize power in a coup
